title: Grill — Issue #298: Chrome browser prompt + bundled-tmux terminal
summary:
Issue #298 has **two independent defects**, and the plan would otherwise make **nine decisions** silently: **four blocking** (scope, how broad the new prompt matcher is, whether Agetor may ever answer the Chrome prompt for the user, and where the bundled tmux gets terminfo), **four that shape the change** (how far the terminfo override reaches, what the user sees on failure, the conditional dismiss action, and the acceptance bar), and **one minor** card-presentation call, plus a four-item confirm list.

The investigation already proved the hard parts: the current matcher chain returns `unparsable: true` with zero choices on the exact unnumbered Chrome prompt; the existing private `parseUnnumberedConsentChoices` parses it; and `TERMINFO_DIRS=/usr/share/terminfo` fixes the exact `can't find terminfo database` error. Those are in **Proven** below — read them first so you don't re-decide them.

Source: issue #298 and `docs/plans/issue-298-chrome-prompt-investigation.md`.

proven.text: **The current chain cannot read the Chrome prompt.** `pickScrapeMatch` has no unnumbered-menu matcher, so the boot footer arm registers the `unparsable: true` card with `choices: []`. A scratch spike against the reporter's pane shape returned exactly that.

evidence.label: the shared chain, used by the runtime scraper and the boot poller
spike: current chain → unparsable, zero choices

proven.text: **The parser already exists and parses it.** `parseUnnumberedConsentChoices` anchors on `Enter to confirm`, walks up over the choice rows, and returns two choices with the cursor on `No`. It is private and reachable only from `matchStartupConsentDialog` (the trust/bypass auto-confirmer), which is why the Chrome prompt never gets choices.

evidence.label: the only caller: numbered first, unnumbered fallback
the parser (private, 2+ contiguous rows, exactly one cursor)

proven.text: **The footer is on the pane but hidden in the card.** `matchUnparsableModal` only fires at boot through its footer arm, so the reporter's pane carried a recognized footer; `cleanPromptPane` strips any line beginning `enter to confirm`, which is why the screenshot's card shows only the two rows.

evidence.label: the unparsable card's preview runs through cleanPromptPane

proven.text: **The terminal failure is the bundled ncurses, not the session.** The bundled tmux links `@executable_path/libncursesw.6.dylib`, whose compiled-in default terminfo dir is the build machine's `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/ncurses/6.5/share/terminfo`; the bundle ships no terminfo. The exact `can't find terminfo database` error reproduces under a pty when that subtree is hidden, and `TERMINFO_DIRS=/usr/share/terminfo` makes the same attach succeed, even against a server started with the broken path.

**Answering already resumes the task.** The answer route validates the clicked key against the registered choices and calls `dismissTmuxPrompt` (arrows + Enter); the `__external__` sweep clears the card once the pane changes; the boot wait re-arms while a prompt is pending. No new interaction kind or resume plumbing is needed.

evidence.label: route: validate key, deliver, mark answered
boot wait re-arms while a startup prompt is pending

proven.text: **The Chrome prompt is a persistent Claude setting, not an Agetor setting.** Claude's docs: `Yes, use my browser` turns browser tools on and connects the logged-in browser; `No, keep browser tools off` or Esc turns the setting off and Claude stops offering Chrome setup. The existing test deliberately does not auto-confirm it.

evidence.label: existing test: never auto-confirm the Chrome prompt

proven.text: **No schema or migration.** The prompt is ephemeral (an in-memory interaction); the terminal fix is runtime-only. There are no rows to backfill.
**No e2e can reach this.** The fake Claude driver bypasses tmux, so pane matchers and Terminal.app attach are unit/manual surfaces only.

sections.title: Scope & the prompt
sections.intro: These decide what the change is and the risk class of the new matcher. The terminal half has its own section.

questions.title: Which halves of issue #298 does this change fix?
questions.why: Decides whether the plan has one workstream or two, and whether the reported fallback stays broken.
questions.context: The issue reports **(A)** the Chrome prompt is unanswerable in Agetor and **(B)** the **Open in Terminal** fallback dies with `can't find terminfo database`. The investigation proved they are independent: (A) is a matcher gap, (B) is the bundled tmux's ncurses lookup. The issue's Expected Behavior asks for both, and its author says either one alone would leave the task stuck.

options.label: Both, one local commit
options.description: Parser + terminal fallback + the terminal error feedback in one change.
options.consequence: One plan, one commit with `Fixes #298`; the largest review surface but the issue is finished as reported.

options.label: Both, two local commits
options.description: One commit for the prompt, one for the terminal fallback.
options.consequence: Easier review and revert; the second commit carries `Fixes #298`; the plan has two waves and must keep them independently green.

options.label: Prompt parser only
options.description: Fix the card; file a separate issue for the terminal.
options.consequence: The reporter can answer the Chrome prompt, but the unparsable card's terminal fallback still dies for bundled-tmux users.

options.label: Terminal fallback only
options.description: Fix the attach; leave the prompt unparsable.
options.consequence: The user must always go to the terminal; the primary complaint (no way to answer in Agetor) stays.

recommendation.reason: The issue asks for both, the halves are small and independent, and one commit keeps the `Fixes #298` link unambiguous.

questions.title: How broad should the new unnumbered-menu matcher be?
questions.why: Sets the false-positive class and how many future Claude menus become readable.
questions.context: The Chrome dialog is an unnumbered Ink select: `❯ No, keep browser tools off` / `  Yes, use my browser` / `Enter to confirm · Esc keep browser tools off`. The same `er` select family already produced the 2.1.284 workspace-trust dialog, which Agetor drives with `Down` + `Enter`. A generic matcher can reuse `parseUnnumberedConsentChoices`, but it also parses a transcript that quotes such a menu. The investigation's proposed guards: footer in the last 3 non-blank lines, exactly one cursor row, 2+ contiguous plain rows, reject checkbox/value-selector rows, and gate on `!paneWorking` and `!paneIdle`. It would sit after the slider and before the unparsable fallback. It only **presents** choices; it never auto-answers.

evidence.label: the only Chrome fixture is the OLD numbered shape — no test covers the unnumbered one

options.label: Generic matcher with strict guards
options.description: Footer-anchored, one cursor row, 2+ contiguous rows, reject checkbox/slider rows, `!paneWorking`, `!paneIdle`.
options.consequence: Any future same-shaped menu becomes answerable; adds a small false-positive class that needs a negative-test matrix.

options.label: Marker-gated for Chrome only
options.description: Match `Claude in Chrome extension detected` (and optionally `Claude wants to use your browser`) only.
options.consequence: Narrowest risk; the next unnumbered menu still lands on the unparsable card.

options.label: Generic + a Chrome marker fallback
options.description: Run the generic matcher, and also parse the Chrome dialog by its header even if the footer wording changes.
options.consequence: Most robust for the reporter's exact CLI; the most code, markers, and tests.

recommendation.reason: The parser already exists and the same Ink component family has now produced two unnumbered dialogs; the strict guards keep the false-positive class bounded, and the matcher only presents choices.

questions.title: Should Agetor ever answer the Chrome browser-tools prompt for the user?
questions.why: Agetor would be changing a persistent Claude setting that controls access to the user's logged-in browser.
questions.context: Claude's docs say **Yes, use my browser** turns browser tools on and connects the session; **No, keep browser tools off** or Esc turns the setting off and Claude stops offering Chrome setup. It is stored in Claude's own config as a one-time policy, not per task. The existing test explicitly asserts the boot auto-confirmer does **not** touch it (`claude-tmux-scraper.test.ts:430`). The investigation's position: the card must present the choice, never choose it.

evidence.label: STARTUP_CONSENT_DIALOGS: only choices the user already made

options.label: Always show the card; never auto-answer
options.description: The user clicks Yes or No; no Agetor setting, no silent default.
options.consequence: The user decides every time Claude shows the dialog; no new settings surface.

options.label: Add an Agetor Settings preference (ask / on / off)
options.description: Agetor pre-answers from a preference the user set.
options.consequence: One-click for repeat users, but Agetor owns a Claude policy and must write/keys Claude's state; brittle across CLI versions.

options.label: Auto-answer No
options.description: Never block; keep browser tools off.
options.consequence: Tasks never stall on it, but every user permanently loses Chrome integration unless they re-enable it in Claude.

options.label: Auto-answer Yes
options.description: Connect the user's browser automatically.
options.consequence: Connects a logged-in browser without consent; not defensible.

recommendation.reason: Both answers change a persistent Claude setting; only the user can make that choice, and the issue only asks for a way to answer it.

sections.title: The terminal fallback
sections.intro: The reported error is environmental, so the source and the blast radius matter more than the command string.

questions.title: Where should the bundled tmux get its terminfo database?
questions.why: Decides whether the fix is a one-line env override or a new vendored asset with build/signing work.
questions.context: The bundle ships `tmux` + `libncursesw.6.dylib` but no terminfo. The dylib's compiled-in default is the build machine's `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/ncurses/6.5/share/terminfo`; when absent, the attach under a tty prints exactly `can't find terminfo database`. Spike: `TERMINFO_DIRS=/usr/share/terminfo` fixes it, including against a server started with the broken path. `/usr/share/terminfo` is present on macOS and has `xterm-256color`, `screen-256color`, and `tmux-256color`.

evidence.label: spike: exact error and the `TERMINFO_DIRS` fix

options.label: Use the macOS system database
options.description: `TERMINFO_DIRS=/usr/share/terminfo` for the affected spawns.
options.consequence: No bundle weight, verified on macOS 26.6.2. Depends on the OS directory staying present.

options.label: Vendor a terminfo database
options.description: Copy a DB into `vendor/tmux/arm64/terminfo` and point the bundled tmux at it.
options.consequence: Fully self-contained; adds files, a source/license to track, a build step, and bundle weight.

options.label: System DB first, vendored DB as fallback
options.description: Search the system DB, then a bundled one.
options.consequence: Most robust; the most work and the most files.

recommendation.reason: Verified present and sufficient, adds no bundle weight, and the defect is a missing build-machine path rather than a missing OS capability.

questions.title: Which tmux surfaces should get the terminfo override?
questions.why: Decides whether this is a one-line attach fix or a helper applied across every bundled-tmux and shell path.
questions.context: The same hardcoded lookup affects any invocation with a tty: the Terminal.app attach (the reported path), a user-typed `tmux attach` in Agetor's in-app terminal (`terminals.ts` forces `TERM=xterm-256color`), and the `agetor attach` CLI (`attach.ts` uses bare `tmux` or `AGETOR_TMUX_BIN`). Headless core calls have no tty and do not resolve terminfo, so they are unaffected either way. `POST /tasks/:id/open-tmux` is app-only; `GET /tmux-source` already exposes `resolvedBin` to the CLI.

options.label: Only the app's Open in Terminal attach
options.description: Set the override in the `do script` command.
options.consequence: Smallest diff; fixes the report, but a bundled-tmux user typing `tmux attach` in Agetor's terminal or `agetor attach` can still hit it.

options.label: The attach + every bundled-tmux spawn
options.description: A tmux-specific env helper, applied only when the source is bundled.
options.consequence: Keeps the bundled path honest; headless calls are unaffected. Adds a helper and tests.

options.label: Also Agetor's in-app terminal shell
options.description: Export the override into the terminal PTY env.
options.consequence: Covers a user-typed attach in Agetor; changes the user shell's environment.

options.label: Also make `agetor attach` resolve `resolvedBin`
options.description: The CLI asks `/tmux-source` for the binary and sets the same env.
options.consequence: Covers the CLI; touches a separate command, its error path, and its tests.

recommendation.reason: Fixes the report and the class (any bundled tmux with a tty) without changing the user's shell env or the CLI contract.

questions.title: How much failure feedback should Open in Terminal give?
questions.why: The issue asks for a recoverable error, but osascript cannot see a failure that happens inside the terminal shell.
questions.context: The current route spawns `/usr/bin/osascript`, returns `{ ok: true }` immediately, and only logs a non-zero exit. The harness terminal route directly above it awaits osascript with a 5 s ceiling and returns a 502 with an Automation-permission hint. Even an awaited osascript returns 0 as soon as Terminal accepts the command, so the reported terminfo failure is invisible to the route; the terminfo fix removes that specific failure.

options.label: Await osascript and return 502
options.description: Mirror the harness route: 5 s ceiling, 502 with the Automation hint.
options.consequence: Catches launch/Automation failures; an in-shell failure still just closes the window.

options.label: Await + keep the window open on failure
options.description: Drop `exec` and append a `|| { printf …; read …; }` fallback to the attach command.
options.consequence: An in-shell failure leaves a readable message and an open window; one extra shell on success.

options.label: Await + add a Copy attach command fallback
options.description: The card offers the exact command for any terminal.
options.consequence: The user can always paste it; extra UI state and a new action.

options.label: Add a PTY preflight before opening
options.description: Probe terminfo with a real PTY before the Terminal window.
options.consequence: Catches the failure before the window; more machinery and possible false negatives.

recommendation.reason: The route can only see osascript's exit, while the reported failure is inside the shell; a one-line fallback keeps the error visible and satisfies the issue's recoverable-error ask.

sections.title: Card UX & acceptance
sections.intro: Presentation and how we prove it. The dismiss question only applies if you chose a generic matcher above.

questions.title: How should the choice card present an unnumbered menu?
questions.why: The card must look like Agetor's own UI, but the real TUI has no numbers and the footer that explains Esc is stripped.
questions.context: The generic card renders `${key}. ${label}`. For the unnumbered Chrome dialog the real TUI has no numbers; the synthetic `1.`/`2.` are Agetor's convention (the slider does the same). `cleanPromptPane` strips `Enter to confirm · Esc keep browser tools off`, so the card shows the dialog body but not Esc's meaning. The dialog body itself says `Turn browser tools off for future sessions with /chrome`.

options.label: Keep the numbered-button convention
options.description: Render `1. No…` / `2. Yes…` like every other choice card.
options.consequence: No new flag or plumbing; the card looks consistent with the slider.

options.label: Hide the synthetic keys for unnumbered menus
options.description: Add a `hideKeys` flag through `ScrapeMatch` → `TmuxPromptRequest` → the webview.
options.consequence: Matches the real dialog; one more field threaded through the prompt plumbing.

options.label: Add a permanence note for the Chrome prompt
options.description: A one-line note that this choice changes Claude's browser-tools setting permanently.
options.consequence: Clearer consequence; needs a Chrome marker or a per-prompt note mechanism.

options.label: Add an Open in Terminal button to choice cards
options.description: An alternative answer path from the same card.
options.consequence: Useful if a click fails; an extra action per card.

recommendation.reason: Lowest surface and consistent with the slider; the dialog body already tells the user browser tools stay off for future sessions.

questions.title: Should the choice card gain a Dismiss (Esc) action?
questions.why: A generic matcher can false-positive; without a dismiss the only way out is clicking a choice (which sends keys) or changing the pane.
questions.context: The generic card has no dismiss; the plan card has `Reject — don't approve` (Esc). For the Chrome dialog, **Esc means `No, keep browser tools off`** — a permanent setting — so a Dismiss labelled `not now` would silently turn Chrome off. The strict matcher and the external sweep are the current safety nets.

options.label: Keep no dismiss
options.description: Rely on the strict matcher; answer in the terminal via Task Details if a card is wrong.
options.consequence: No risk of an accidental permanent No; a false-positive card needs a choice click or a terminal.

options.label: Add Dismiss with a Chrome warning
options.description: Dismiss sends Esc, with an explicit warning on the Chrome card that Esc = No/permanent.
options.consequence: A safety valve; more UI and a prompt-specific warning.

options.label: Add Dismiss except for Chrome
options.description: Marker-gate the Chrome prompt out of the dismiss path.
options.consequence: A safety valve where Esc is safe; needs a marker to exclude Chrome.

recommendation.reason: The only current unnumbered prompt has a destructive Esc; the matcher guards are the safer place to spend risk.

questions.title: What counts as done for this change?
questions.why: Sets the test and manual-smoke bar; the fake driver means e2e cannot reach either defect.
questions.context: `bun test` covers the matcher and a pure attach-command builder. The Chrome dialog needs a fresh Chrome-onboarding state to live-drive; this machine already has `claudeInChromeDefaultEnabled: true`, and the fake Claude driver bypasses tmux. The installed Agetor bundle can be used for a manual attach smoke, but it is a GUI/Terminal.app action.

options.label: Units + typecheck + a manual Terminal smoke
options.description: Fixture-based prompt tests, a pure attach-builder test, and one real Open in Terminal attach (documented if the environment can't run it).
options.consequence: Proves the parser and the command; the terminal path gets a real smoke when the environment allows.

options.label: Units + typecheck only
options.description: No GUI smoke.
options.consequence: Fastest; the Terminal.app path stays unverified until the user tries it.

options.label: Also live-drive the Chrome prompt
options.description: Use a fresh Claude Chrome-onboarding state/temp home to see the real dialog.
options.consequence: Strongest; needs credentials and home manipulation and may not be possible here.

recommendation.reason: The parser is deterministic and unit-testable; the terminal defect is environmental and deserves one real attach.

sections.title: Confirm or override
sections.intro: Low-stakes defaults I'd bet on. Confirm with one click, or override if you disagree.

questions.title: Update the docs that describe this behavior

recommendation.value: Yes — update `docs/architecture/harness-claude-code.md` (matcher chain + attach env), the `docs/plans/unknown-claude-prompts-fallback.md` addendum, and the manual QA row `docs/qa/master-token-agent-read-qa.md:53-54`.
recommendation.reason: These are the current written description of the scraper and the attach path; leaving them stale is how the next agent re-learns it the hard way.

recommendation.value: One local commit, not pushed, message `fix: answer the unnumbered Claude Chrome prompt and repair bundled-tmux attach (Fixes #298)`.
recommendation.reason: The pipeline requires a local commit mentioning `Fixes #298`; the user reviews and pushes it.

questions.title: Keep the unparsable card as the final fallback

recommendation.value: Yes — genuinely unknown prompts still get the `unparsable` card with its Open in Terminal action.
recommendation.reason: The new matcher only covers one shape; the fallback is what keeps the next unknown widget recoverable.

recommendation.value: Yes — this change only makes the Claude startup prompt answerable; it does not coordinate Chrome between Codex, Claude Desktop, and Agetor.
recommendation.reason: The prompt is a one-time Claude setting, not a Chrome lock; cross-agent coordination is a different feature with a different owner.
